name: LiteTV Channels
description: Lightweight virtual TV channels: deterministic schedules over your own library, tuned in via normal direct playback at the live position. No transcoding, no tuner emulation.
overview: TV channels from your library, without transcoding.

versions.changelog: Kanalvorschläge urteilen jetzt über Ähnlichkeit statt nur über das Studio: ein Pool wird zusätzlich auf den Titel getrimmt, um den er überwiegend geht – gemessen mit Smart Similar, mit einem groben Rückfall, wenn dieses Plugin fehlt oder nicht antwortet. Ein DreamWorks-Sender hält damit keinen Thriller mehr neben Animationsfilmen, nur weil beide vom selben Studio sind. Der Filmabend eines Vorschlags verwendet nun eigens reservierte Filme statt der Kanalinhalte selbst, sodass kein Titel doppelt läuft; ein reiner Filmkanal bekommt gar keinen Filmabend mehr. Dazu vier weitere Einstellungen – Ähnlichkeitsstrenge, Filmabend immer/passend/nie, Trailer und Folgenmischen einzeln, sowie Mindest- und Höchstzahl der Quellen – und eine aufklappbare Titelliste je Vorschlag vor dem Hinzufügen.

Fertige Kanalvorschläge lassen sich jetzt steuern: Bibliotheken ein- oder ausschließen, eine Altersgruppe wählen, die Kanalgröße über einen Regler begrenzen – gezählt in abspielbaren Titeln, also Folgen statt Serien – und die gewünschten Kanalarten auswählen. Jeder Vorschlag nennt Altersband, Studios oder Genres, Bibliotheken und seine geschätzte Größe, bevor er hinzugefügt wird; ein Entwurf, der nicht in die erlaubte Größe passt, wird gar nicht erst angeboten. Ein Kanal wird auf die Altersgruppe getrimmt, um die er überwiegend geht, damit kein Jugend-Actionsender Vorschulserien über ein gemeinsames Studio oder ein gemeinsames Genrewort einsammelt. Studio-Sender für Disney, DreamWorks, Marvel, Warner, Nickelodeon und Cartoon Network erscheinen nur, wenn die Metadaten sie belegen. »Andere Ideen zeigen« liefert wirklich andere Vorschläge, und eine abgelehnte Idee kommt nicht zurück. Außerdem: die Altersangabe des Herkunftsnachweises ist jetzt so formuliert wie die übrigen Zeitangaben der Seite.

Fertige Kanalvorschläge bauen nun aus der eigenen Bibliothek komplette Sender: lokale Quellen mit einer echten 100%-Gewichtung, gemischte Serienfolgen, Trailer-Vorschau, passendes geliehenes Artwork und – bei genügend Filmen – einen samstäglichen Filmabend um 20:15 ohne Leerlauf. Vorschläge wie Werkstatt & Wildnis, Kinderzeit, Disney & Pixar (nur bei passenden Studio-Metadaten) und Genre-Sender sind bewusst keine Kopien echter Sender. Die bisherigen Wege zum Erstellen aus Lieblingstiteln sowie aus Bibliothek und Genres bleiben unverändert; Sammlungs-Marathons sind ebenfalls weiter verfügbar.

Source probabilities are now a true 100% distribution. Editing one percentage proportionally adjusts the others; removing a source redistributes its share, and new sources start at 0% so they never silently change an existing channel.

Film night now resumes with the next complete episode after the film, never a short tail of the episode before it. Shorter series repeat within a channel cycle until the longest series has completed once, so all configured series remain present through the week. The schedule grid now shows series name and episode title together.

Fixes weighted random scheduling: every draw, including the first, uses the selected block size; a source cannot immediately repeat while another positively weighted source still has episodes. The configuration preview now follows exactly the same rule.

Weighted random can now shuffle episodes within each chosen series while retaining the source probabilities and block size. Film night shows the actual selected film length, never cuts an episode for a scheduled film, and can move the film start up to 30 minutes to finish the current programme cleanly without a lead-in gap.

Weighted random scheduling now assigns a probability to each source and draws a fresh source for every block. The 'some at a time' setting controls how many episodes are appended from the selected source; the configuration preview follows the same rule.

Clarifies source-aware random scheduling: each series is shuffled independently, sources remain in their configured order, and the 'some at a time' setting always takes exactly that many episodes from each source before moving on. The content-page preview now refreshes when any scheduling option changes, including same-source probability.

Refines random scheduling into three clear modes: in-order playback, independently shuffled sources distributed in the configured episode groups, and weighted random playback that can prefer the current source with a configurable probability while ignoring episode-group sizing. The modern and legacy configuration previews now use the same semantics.

Die Tagesansicht kann jetzt durch alle Tage der ausgewählten Woche navigieren. Online-Bilder bleiben nach dem Speichern erhalten. Block-Trailer folgen bei wechselnden Filmabend-Filmen automatisch dem Film der jeweiligen Woche.

Der Schedule-Anfang lässt sich jetzt minutengenau mit Sekunden setzen; ein Button schlägt eine passende volle Stunde vor. Die Inhaltsvorschau folgt nun der Server-Reihenfolge, ausgewählte Starttitel bleiben erhalten und Wochenblöcke sind im Schedule farblich hervorgehoben.

Channels werden sofort gespeichert, während die Schedule-Erzeugung im Hintergrund läuft. Collections aus der Titelsuche werden als echte Quellen erkannt, und die Bibliotheksansicht hat für große Bibliotheken eine Suchleiste. Die doppelte Spracheinstellung wurde entfernt.

**Collections können jetzt direkt als einzige Channel-Quelle verwendet werden.** YouTube-Quellen zeigen wieder passende Vorschaubilder, sofern YouTube sie bereitstellt. Außerdem wurde die doppelte Beschriftung **Sprache der Konfigurationsseite** entfernt und die Servereinstellung korrekt als **Wiedergabe & Trailer** bezeichnet.

**Kanal- und Servereinstellungen werden automatisch gespeichert.** Mehrere Änderungen können mit **Änderungen zurücksetzen** gemeinsam auf den Stand beim Öffnen der Seite zurückgesetzt werden. Das Löschen eines Channels bleibt sofort endgültig. Die Sprache der Konfigurationsseite wird nur noch unter den Servereinstellungen angezeigt.
Restores the stable v1.0.97 baseline while retaining trailer scheduling, remote trailers, playlist previews and collection order. Uses a simple direct German/English language switch.

**Trailer scheduling is configurable again in the new Breaks screen.** Preview, manual-title and combined modes are available, with a library search for the titles used by Manual and Both. Zero really means no automatic trailer insertion.

**Trailer settings now apply to programme blocks as well as the base lineup.** Scheduled local trailers retain their trailer identity through week generation and are shown as trailers in the stored schedule. Collections can supply their children's local trailer files when the collection itself has none.

**The configuration app was rebuilt and the existing trailer behaviour is covered by the release checks.

**A YouTube playlist can be added to a channel again.** Pasting a link into the Content list put a row on it, and then Save answered **HTTP 400** and nothing was written - not the link and not any other change to that channel. The page wrote the link's source with an empty id where the server wants a real one; the server could not read the body at all, so it refused the whole channel before any of it was looked at. Links carry the empty id properly now, and adding one, saving, and reading it back is checked against a real server before every release.

**A selected row can be let go of.** Selecting a row in the Content list is what arms the keyboard - Delete removes it, Alt with an arrow moves it - and the only ways to un-select were clicking that exact row again or finding the thin strip of list below the last one. Clicking anywhere else on the page left the row marked selected with the keyboard nowhere near it. Turning your attention elsewhere now lets it go: a click anywhere outside the list, or tabbing out of it. Escape still does it too, and the bar's own Move and Remove buttons do not count as leaving.

**Series come before episodes in search.** Films, series, collections and episodes were asked for in one request, so the server decided the order and put episodes wherever relevance landed them - a series' own episodes above the series itself, and for a long-running show, twenty episodes and no series row at all. The two are asked for separately now: titles first, in the server's own order, and the episodes after them.

**The channel-list preview's words fit the row again.** The row was given the television's real proportions last release - 78dp tall with the banner beside it - which makes it a sliver about thirty pixels high, and the four lines of text inside it kept the sizes they had when it was three times taller. They ran over each other. Everything in the row is now a share of its height, taken from the app: the name, what is on, the progress bar and what is next, all at the app's own sizes.

**One search bar, not two, and it finds all five kinds.** The shelf and the Content list each had a box for titles and a second box beside it for addresses — and on the shelf the second one carried a "Put on the shelf" button that stood there whether there was anything to put or not. There is one box on each screen now. Type a title and it searches; paste a link and it reads it, says whether it is a playlist and how many videos are in it, and offers it as a row in the same list.

**Episodes can be found by name.** Searching only ever looked at films, series and collections, so the only way to reach an episode was to know which series it was in, find that, and open it. Type "Bärengebiet" now and you get the episode, with the series it belongs to and its season and episode number beside it so a list of episodes from four different series is still readable. On the shelf it drags straight onto the week; on the Content list it can be the channel's content on its own. A series still opens if browsing is what you want.

Nothing about scheduling changed to allow that: an episode was always playable, it simply had no name of its own in the list of things a source can be, so the page had to call it a film or leave it out.

**The backdrop preview was showing the poster.** Yesterday's rebuilt "On the television" card added the cover beside the channel's name, inside the television frame - and the rule that stretches the backdrop across that frame was written loosely enough to catch it too. So the poster was blown up over the whole preview, the words were hidden underneath it, and the picture sitting under "your backdrop" was not the backdrop at all. The owner saw it immediately: "what is the giant poster crop doing there on the backdrop place". It draws the backdrop now, with the channel's name, what is on, the Watch live button and the guide column over it, as the television does.

**And the channel-list row shows the banner at a banner's shape.** The row let its words decide how tall it was and stretched the picture to match, which came out at about three to one - a crop the television never makes, in the one preview whose whole job is the crop. The row now has the app's own proportions, the picture takes its true share of the width, and what you see cut off is what will be cut off.

**The "On the television" preview now draws what the television draws.** It was invented rather than measured, and three things about it were wrong. The channel-list card was a wide picture with the name laid over it; the app has no such screen - it draws a row with the words on the left and the picture on the right at a banner's shape, and nothing is ever written over the artwork there. The channel screen's frame was a fixed band about four to one, so every picture was cropped to a shape the television never crops it to, and then judged on that crop; it is 16:9 now, and it shows the app's own two-layer wash, including the fact that the right of the picture is **not** dimmed because the guide sits over it. And the card offered a poster as a stand-in for the wide picture, which the app never does - a poster cannot reach the list card at all. The words under each preview now also say that whatever is on air is tried **before** your other picture, not after, which is the order the app actually uses.

**An uploaded picture nobody points at any more is deleted.** Uploading wrote a file and handed the page an address; clearing the slot, replacing the picture, or borrowing a title's artwork instead only ever changed the address, so the file stayed on the server with nothing referring to it and no way to remove it. Deleting a channel left all three of its pictures behind too. Both are cleaned up now - on the save rather than when a slot is cleared, so an abandoned edit cannot destroy a picture the stored channel still uses.

**The zoom scale now reaches the rule "Zoom to now" is asked to obey.** With the rule in 1.0.90.0 - a third of the view for the programme on air, and never less than about half an hour of schedule on screen - a short programme asks for about 1500 pixels an hour, and the slider stopped at 1200. So the ask fell off the end of the scale, the slider pinned at its maximum, and a four-minute trailer still got the most zoomed-in view the page had. The scale runs to 2400 now and the wanted zoom is reachable. The three hand-written copies of the slider's bounds - the store, the slider itself and the clamp - are one exported pair.

**"Zoom to now" follows the owner's rule: a third of the view for the programme on air, two thirds for what runs before and after it, and the programme in the middle rather than wherever a fixed offset left it.** It used to give every programme a fixed 55% of the height whatever its length, which for a three-minute advert asked for some seven thousand pixels an hour, pinned the slider at its maximum and left one bar on the screen with nothing around it to say where in the evening it sat. There is a floor on context now - never less than about half an hour of schedule on screen - so a short programme takes less than its third and gets more neighbours than it asked for, which is the right way round. A programme longer than the view is still centred, but not so far that the now line leaves the screen.

**The zoom really works now.** 1.0.88.0 tidied the zoom into one source and split the toggles, which was worth doing, but it did not fix the bug: the slider still did nothing. The cause was one word. The store held the current channel in a plain field rather than a reactive one, so everything keyed off the channel - the zoom, both toggles, and the grid's own height - was worked out once while there was no channel yet and never worked out again. The slider wrote a real number under a real channel and the grid went on reading a key that had been empty when it last looked. Switching to Week and back "helped" because the view *was* reactive, and was the only thing that could make the grid look again.

**The zoom slider works, and there are two toggles instead of one.**

The slider did nothing on the Day view - switching to Week and back "helped" - because the zoom had two sources: a worked-out one and the slider's, and the code preferred the worked-out one, which is the opposite of what it was written to do. Whichever won depended on the order things happened to run in. There is one source now, and the slider writes to it.

**Follow what's on** now only decides *where* the grid is scrolled - it brings the now line into view and, the part that was missing, **keeps it in view while you zoom**.

**Zoom to now** is a new box that decides *how big* things are: the programme on air fills a good half of the view, so a channel of forty short items and a channel of four films both open readable. It re-sizes when the window does, and a hand on the slider unticks it. The two used to be one box doing both jobs, so wanting either without the other was impossible.

**The shelf and the selected-programme bar were unreachable on the Week screen, and that was a regression in 1.0.84.0.** Stopping the grid from collapsing while a channel loads meant wrapping it in a plain container - and the grid is written to take the column's leftover height and scroll inside itself, so the wrapper broke that: the grid grew to its full natural height, thousands of pixels of it, the page stopped scrolling, and everything below it was pushed somewhere nobody could reach. Both were still being drawn; there was simply no way to get to them. The wrapper now carries the grid's own sizing.

**A playlist channel showed two titles that contradicted each other.** A YouTube playlist source was named by a description the page composed - "16 videos - <the first video's title>" - and the schedule then carried that under every programme as its series, so the app drew "7 vs. Wild Folge 3" with "16 videos - 7 vs. Wild - The Beginning | Episode 1" beneath it. It reads as a channel airing the wrong thing, and was reported as exactly that. The playlist's own name is read from YouTube now. **Playlists added before this keep the old name until they are added again** - or just rename the source.

**The schedule says when things air.** A block tall enough for two lines now carries its start and end time above its name, instead of keeping them in a tooltip a television cannot show. **And the times down the left are clock times** - `00:00`, `02:00` - rather than the bare `00 02 04 06`, which read as an axis on a chart instead of the time of day.

**YouTube answers in your language now.** Every request the plugin made said `hl=en, gl=US`, written into two files - so a German household read an English schedule for videos that have perfectly good German titles. YouTube localises a title and hands back the original where there is no translation, so asking in German costs nothing and loses nothing. It follows the language the configuration page is set to, and there is a field on Server settings - **Ask YouTube in** - that takes any language tag.

**An advert nobody named is called what YouTube calls it**, not `aqz-KE-bpKQ`. The title arrives on the same answer as the length, so it costs no extra request.

A test now fails the build if any code asks YouTube in a hard-coded language again.

A wall of pictures standing in for banners searched **in your library** said "no provider had a true banner", which is the wrong half of the screen - no provider was asked. It says the titles hold no banner, which is what happened.

**The channels are stored one file each.** They used to be a list inside the plugin's single configuration document, which is how one bad value made *every* channel unsaveable last release: the document either reads or it does not. Now a channel the server cannot read costs that one channel and says so in the log, saving one channel cannot touch another, and a page left open cannot undo somebody else's edit by posting a whole list back over it. Existing channels are moved across on first start - written out and read back before the old list is cleared, so nothing is lost if anything goes wrong.

**A new channel arrives with its week already laid out.** Making one from a suggested lineup used to leave a blank schedule until you found "Lay this week out", which nothing told you about. The same Save that creates the channel now lays it out.

**Nothing on the schedule moves when you click it.** Selecting a programme used to make the Undo and Discard buttons appear and "Lay this week out" grow into "Save and lay this week out", so every button after them shifted and the one under the pointer was no longer the one that had been there. The space is reserved now, here and on the two other buttons that did it.

**Switching channels no longer makes the page jump.** The schedule was replaced by a single line of text while the next week was fetched, collapsing a screenful and blowing it back up a moment later. The grid stays where it is.

**A picture standing in for a banner is shown at its own shape.** Where no true banner exists the wall fell back to the widest picture there is but still drew it five-to-one, so you were asked to choose and crop a picture you could not see. The stand-ins now get a wall of their own, at their own shape, under a line saying why they are there.

The plugin strip no longer lists SponsorBlock Segments, Next Up Cleanup or Clear Transcodes: LiteTV does not use any of them.
